title: H1 injectivity makes the Picard triviality locus open
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ and $f_i:X_i\to S$ ($1\le i\le n$) be flat, proper morphisms of finite presentation [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-scheme-over-base, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and let $u_i:X_i\to X$ be morphisms over $S$. Assume that for every morphism $T\to S$, the canonical maps $\mathcal O_T\to (f_T)_*\mathcal O_{X_T}$ and $\mathcal O_T\to ((f_i)_T)_*\mathcal O_{(X_i)_T}$ are isomorphisms [def-pc-base-change, lem-sc-picard-diagonal-locally-closed]. Let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible module on $X$ [def-sc-invertible-module], let $\mathcal L_i=u_i^*\mathcal L$ be its pullback to $X_i$ [def-pc-module-pullback], and let $Z$ and $Z_i$ be the locally closed subschemes of $S$ representing the loci where $\mathcal L$ and $\mathcal L_i$ are pulled back from the base. Assume $Z$ is contained in the scheme-theoretic intersection of the $Z_i$. If $s\in Z$ and the map $H^1(X_s,\mathcal O_{X_s})\to\bigoplus_i H^1((X_i)_s,\mathcal O_{(X_i)_s})$ induced by the morphisms $u_i$ is injective, then there is an open neighbourhood $U$ of $s$ in $S$ such that $Z\cap U$ equals $(\bigcap_i Z_i)\cap U$ scheme-theoretically.
